entries.text: Would that be the right size for a mill pond?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, I think so.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Because these logs were only 16 foot long or so.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. And that basin went on around the corner, didn't it, from here?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah. See that depression over there on the Smith Peak side there, could that be the type of place they'd yard logs out of?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, they didn't actually yard them out. They just put three logs together, two on the sides and one on the bottom, and then cabled them. And of course the wet logs would lubricate the log chute and they'd pull them right into the mill, directly into the mill from the pond. By the way, Clifford Cornutt is going to be up here probably within the next year or so. And when he does he's going to look me up. Might be interesting to see what he remembers. Like I say, he left here when he was in 3rd grade. He was pretty young.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Will you be coming up to these mill areas here with Clifford?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Very likely.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, that might be good to get either me or Jeff Garver or somebody involved at that time from the school.

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: U. Berry Creek Schoolhouse

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, we're driving past the spring that's between the 200 Road turnoff, where we've been looking at the first two Coote sites, and the bottom of the hill here. But this is a spring that they opened up.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: They dug this up when they built this road. They tried everything they could to make the spring drain into the gutter or do something with it, and it always came up right in the middle of the road. And that's close to 50 years ago and it's still here!

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you call that the Coote's Mill Road at that time?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That connects up with this road here. Did this road go through at that time?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: This road wasn't here. You see the school house [Berry Creek] was right here.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Right next to where this gate is.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: See the survey marker there?

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The school house sat on the section line, on the south side of the section line. So it sat right here.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. And it took up about an acre?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now there's a couple little fruit trees around through here. Were those here at that time?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The fruit trees were, but there was no sign of a house here.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. Were they raised like an orchard or were they just kind of scattered?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Just scattered like they are now.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Could they have been put there by sheep, or do you think they were planted trees?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It was possible. You've got an apple tree over here. Could have been scattered by sheep. But they seem to be mostly apple trees. But there had to be an apple tree here, maybe Johnny Appleseed planted it.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you recall any road or farm grade or anything along the base of the hill over there?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, there was nothing. I walked all over here and saw all the rattlesnakes on that hill. Which was none. But after the big snow.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's the '37-'38 snow?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. After that we came up here and pulled some wool off the sheep that had died in that snow. So I was pretty much all over that hill. And there was no roads or anything, just sheep trails.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, no roads at all.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, huh uh. And what we did, my mother...

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now, we're looking at Smith Peak from the north side. And on that, at that time, did you call that Folk's Hill?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Really, I think we probably called it Smith's Hill. We didn't really name these hills like you do. I mean we all knew where they were, and you know, basically it was over here or over there you know.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you think. . something that we talked about, with all the families that moved in here in

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: the late '20s and '30s, do you think maybe they lost some of those pioneer names like Savage Creek and Smith Peak?

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I'm sure they did. Of course, like I said, this whole creek system was Berry Creek to me until I talked to you and Donald and so forth. But we always called this Berry Creek. That went past the school house here.

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So we can't blame this on Camp Adair. This is probably just the immigration of people

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: coming in in the '20s and '30s and working with the mill and stuff.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. We used to go over to Berry Creek, or Savage Creek as you call it, to come to school a lot of times during lunch hour, on a nice day like today and eat our lunch over there and stuff. And we all called it Berry Creek. Everybody in school did. But apparently Donald knew it by Savage Creek [See Glender].
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you know if there's any pictures from this angle here -- we're looking from the road towards the bales of hay that's in the second Coote mill site -- are there any pictures when that mill was there of any of the shacks standing that you know of?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. No I don't. I think Coote really stayed on top of that ridge there.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, we're right at the horse trail just beyond the county road oak, there. That oak is the end of the county road. And the new crossing here on Sulphur Springs.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I guess what Bob wants me to tell you, is how he got acquainted with me was that when I was a kid we used to come up to Sulphur Springs and play baseball here on, apparently what was the lot of the old lodge that used to be up here. And we, when we moved from Berry Creek over to Oak Creek, a guy by the name of Charlie White and I herded our cows around from Berry Creek up here to Sulphur Springs and then we went across in back of, that was Peavy Arboretum at that rime, the CCC camp, now it's part of the Oregon State Forestry Department buildings. And on the trip across, I don't know if I recorded it or not, but the CCC boys were from back east some place and they were falling trees like a beaver, just going around and around them, and then when they'd get down to where it was pretty small they'd holler "last round!" and everybody would clear out except the last guy chopping, and he'd chop until he saw which way it was going to go down, and then he'd run the other way. So we got quite a kick out of that, and that's a story I've told quite a few times.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now where were the CCC boys working?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Right up on top of the second ridge up here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now we're right at the mouth of Baker Creek, so it was up towards Oak Creek from here?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: They were coming all the way out from Peavy Arboretum to work?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you know how they came out here?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I think they probably had trucks that they rode in.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did they come along Lewisburg Saddle or come out the way we took?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I think they had their own road through there.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. So they wouldn't have come up Soap Creek.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. No, they. . . i'm quite sure that they were cutting roads and stuff through there, and so forth. Anyway, three or four years ago my daughter wanted to know something about my history, and so I said well let's just take off one of these days and I'll show you things that I did when I was younger. And so we got in the car and we went up to Oak Creek, to the house that we used to live in, and then I took her up to where our pasture used to be, and now it's all planted to houses. And then we went on up as far as we could toward the McDonald Forest here, and then we turned around and we came back around and came to Sulphur Springs and we sat down and
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: ate our lunch at Sulphur Springs. And I was kind of disappointed at the mess that Sulphur Springs had become and the fact that there was no signs so that nobody in the Corvallis area knew where Sulphur Springs was. They all knew about Sulphur Springs Road, but they didn't know there was such a thing as a Sulphur Spring out there. And so I thought that it at least ought to be marked on the road so people could go down and stick their hand in it and make their hand smell rotten for the rest of the day!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you ever drink that spring water?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, but I stuck my hand in it and it sure is hard to get the smell off your hand. But anyway, I was pretty upset that it was in such disrepair, and so I took it upon myself to try and figure out some way to at least get a sign up here. So I went to the county and the county said, well, we can't do anything that belongs to the college and the college just can't cooperate a bit. So I kept looking and nosing around and one thing and another, and I knew this Jeff Garver that I knew worked in the Forestry Department of the College, and he went to the same church as I did. So one day I asked him before Sunday school, I said "Jeff, who would I see to do some work on Sulphur Springs? I'm in the Soil and Water Conservation Board [Benton County] and the Governor has given us $1,000 to do work on streambanks and so forth, and that's to help high school kids out financially and stuff. I'd like to do some cleanup work on it, and I just wondered who I'd see." And he said, "Me." So then we started talking about it, and so then a group of fellows came in to the Soil and Water Conservation Board and wanted a project of surveying and so forth for some work, and so we sucked them into the Sulphur Springs area here, and they drew up maps and the situation as far as trails are concerned, how much they were likely to erode if there were traffic and so forth. And they came up with the idea of coming down a few hundred feet below Sulphur Springs and putting a bridge across for horses and bicycles. And we're sitting right beside that bridge right now. Apparently Jeff Garver has carried it on that far. But while I was here I got some Boy Scouts in here and we
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Who drew up the plans on the bridge?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: They were college kids, I don't know who they were.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Somebody from Oregon State?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And they were funded by the Benton County Soil & Consen'ation Board?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, they weren't funded by us but they were just looking for a project. It was so they could graduate. It was a project for graduating in forestry.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Oh, I see. So it was like a senior project, or.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, they were all seniors, that was their last year. There were three of them in there.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you recall their names?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I don't but I'm sure that. . . I turned in the literature that I had on it back to the Benton County Soil & Conservation Board and they have it on file, I'm sure, and I think that probably Jeff Garver does. Anyway, it turned out that we did. . . Jeff said, I can get all the chips I want for making trails for nothing. So then a Boy Scout Master, he's a lawyer in the old GT building, he came and wanted a job for his scouts. So I got Jeff to dump a load of chips in there and mark out where he wanted the trails and the boys came in here and did the trails and then Jeff came and told me, maybe I
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: shouldn't say this on the tape, he told me we're going to log on the back side of that hill, but because of the fact that you have got it started as a park, we are not going to log on the Sulphur Springs side of the hill. So these trees that you see standing here now, are standing here because of what I had started. Anyway, but Jeff said we'd have to stop the project for a couple of years, because if we try and log and after we did the project there would be weeping and wailing and gnashing of teeth! So it stopped and before it got started again, I moved to Independence. And this is the first time I've been back since and I see that they're doing pretty much what I had planned. And if you would take this trail over this bridge you would find some beaver dams up there and quite a bit of interesting stuff on that trail that you would miss by going across Sulphur Springs.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Our Cultural Resource Inventory [1990 OSU Research Forests "Human Use" Cultural Resource Inventory I recommended that those beaver ponds he opened for interpretation and also Sulphur Springs Trail be developed, so we're behind you on that time wise, but the thinking was in the same place.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, but anyway, that's how this all got started with, because I didn't like the way the place looked. But Jeff had also told me that when we got the work done that they had tractors and rototilers and stuff, and they would go ahead and work this ground up and level it out and reseed the lawn, and so the idea of the bridge is to keep horses and trail bikes and bicycles and stuff out of their new lawn. So that's why it comes around here. Plus the fact that it does go through the beaver pond area and so forth.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was that part of the original planning, that this trail go up to the beaver ponds at that time?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It was going around them, yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So that was part of the plan.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: That was part of the original plan, yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And you say that that plan either Jeff s got a copy of, or the Water Conservation people?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: One or the other. Jeff and the head of the. . . let's see, I'm not sure whether the head of the water resource went with us or not, but there was three of us that walked through here and kind of laid out that trail. But I didn't know about the beaver dams and stuff in there until Jeff told me about them, so Jeff sort of led the way around through here and it was kind of an interesting thing. Apparently those beavers have been in there for a lot of years but I didn't know about them.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: There was literature that the beavers were stocked in Oak Creek in the late 1940s by Oregon State researchers, but i'm not sure that they still know that. And there's no record of any beavers in here before the '40s.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, is that right? Well, that's probably why I never saw any beaver dams up here then.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now you mentioned that you'd come up here to play baseball. How many times did you do that?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Probably three or four.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Would it be like teams, organized baseball?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, just come up here and play. After church. Went to Sunday School, you know.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Would you drive a car all the way back in here?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Urn hmm.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So it was like for picnics and stuff
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, that type of thing. Actually, it was more a boy/girl deal, maybe two carloads of us just come up here for the afternoon and oh just get acquainted more and stuff, you
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: know.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did this par/c have any reputation or anything?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: It was just a place to go for picnics?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, it was a nice level, grassy, area. Apparently was lawn for the lodge when it was here. I didn't know that there was a lodge here until I got involved the second time here, but they tell me that there used to be a lodge there that burned down, and probably that was lawn. But after they had trail bikes and their horses coming over from Corvallis and stuff, they really cut that lawn up and so it's a mess.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did they have any picnic tables here at that time?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't think so.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How about on the fountain, did they have any spout at the fountain or anything?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: It was just a little pool?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It was cleaned out and of course that concrete took care of that.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: It was new in the '30s. Where it said Sulphur Springs.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. And not spelled right if I remember right.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you recall who built that?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I have no idea. Like I say, this area to me was a long ways away. The automobiles we drove then was 40 miles an hour or so, and so I don't know how far it is, but six or eight miles, so it was a half hour drive over here. My dad told me when I was learning to drive for my driver's license he told me that no man should ever drive over 35 miles an hour, that's as fast as a man can think. So, now you know.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So Sulphur Springs was just kind of a special place to come to?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, just something for a change. Kids, you know how kids will be, they've got to go someplace.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you do any fishing through here?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. We had plenty of fishing over there on Berry Creek.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Can you remember what this looked like off to our right here, towards the east?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I Can't. I have no memory of that at all. I was looking at girls, what do you think?!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Well, that's where [Roy] Cook said that they guys from the college brought girls out here for the same thing. I think it was kind of a socializing spot maybe.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, over there on Oak Creek they did a lot of that. I'll show you where we lived on Oak Creek and we had to cross the creek to go home, cross a little bridge, and there was a lot of trees there. And most every time we wanted to go out on Saturday night or Sunday night we had to wait for the kids to get all dressed back up and start their cars and back them out of our road!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Well, let's see. We'll be talking about Charlie White and stuff as we go up and over. Can you think of anything else by this part here? I want to get a picture of the horse bridge and everything before we go.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. I think that Charlie White was a big part of my life in Berry Creek, and maybe, right now, since I mentioned that he went over the hill with me here, and he knew the route, I didn't. He led us over. And I first met Charlie White the first day we moved into Berry Creek. He came over and helped us a little bit and did a lot watching and talking, because like I mentioned before, I had four sisters. And that first day he really painted a beautiful picture of Edith Tandy, who was his niece. And
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: all the time I lived here that stayed with me. Boy, if I saw Edith I'd come all apart. Cause I was just a young fellow and he told me how pretty she was, and what a nice personality she had, and all that stuff. So, anyway, that was my first meeting with Charlie White.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did Edith Tandy live up to her billing?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, I thought so.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So if nothing else, Charlie White was a convincing talker.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, after all, I married an Edith! But anyway, as I look at the pictures of her she isn't near as beautiful as I thought she was. But anyway, to carry Charlie on a little further he was not very anxious to work. Money didn't mean too much to him. Bob mentioned that he was probably a hippy before his time.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I think you put those words in my mouth.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, maybe so, but anyway, he and I did a lot of things together. And for the most part they weren't things that my mother would have been too happy about. But Charlie, he always kind of figured, you know, that if he needed some gas, well he had a Kentucky credit card, which probably people don't know what is now, but it was a siphon hose. And he helped himself to somebody that had some. And one time he came up to our house and told me that he had to have some gas, because his dad his dad was about 80 at that time, and was real sick and he had to get him to the doctor. So he got me to go out to the garage with him and he siphoned some gas out of Bill Coote's Essex! And of course his dad wasn't sick at all but that was just a story he made up. And ultimately he stole some gas from my dad and my dad put him in the penitentiary for a year along with some other people. So we didn't see Charlie for quite a while, and after he got out, well easy money was made like a lot of people that are over in the near east right now thought, it's easy money, so he joined the National Guard. And got that money every month and thought he was really smart, and then World War II came along. So they drafted Charlie into the service and after he'd been in the service for a while, well they discharged him because he had flat feet. But really they discharged him because he spent more than a year in penitentiary and lost his citizenship!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Oh, from stealing the gas?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: From the stealing the gas and stuff.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was he sorry to get out?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, no, he was real happy to get out! That money didn't look nearly so good then. Charlie got into a lot of trouble. He didn't do anything real bad, but he was always just bordering on getting into trouble and so forth. And Halloween night, I think I told you about moving the outhouse and him falling in the hole, didn't 1?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I think we saved all the Charlie White stories for going over Sulphur Springs here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, anyway, the last year that they had Berry Creek in operation, well, we had a Halloween party at the school. Forest Tandy was on the Board of Trustees and so was my dad. And Forest says, "I don't believe those outhouses will stand to be tipped over again, maybe we'd better stay here and watch them." And my dad says, "Well, I've got a busy day tomorrow, why don't you and Neil stay here?" So we stayed there, and Charlie White, and about eight or nine kids were running up and down the road waiting for us to go home; they could see we were there on account of we had a fire in the stove there. So Forest says, "What do you say we move the outhouse off the hole and let the fire go out?' So we did, and they were riding a touring car,
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: which was a car with a rag top that you could fold down, but it had two seats in it. And they were all stacked all over that car and sticking out and so forth. And so they came back after we let the fire go out and they stopped in front of the school and Charlie White says, "Last one out is a nigger baby!" and he took off running and jumped right in the hole. They made him walk home.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How far did he live from there?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, about a half a mile. But anyway, I always kind of laughed about that, because that last one in was a nigger baby and he was it! Then Charlie . . . I was at Gilbert Ennis's one day and we were cutting some wood and Charlie was there. And there was a couple of deaf/mutes working there, and they were going through all kinds of signs and one thing and another, trying to tell us what was going on, and finally a couple of [Oregon] State Police walked up and arrested Charlie!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: They'd been trying to warn you but you couldn't figure it out!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We couldn't figure it out. They were putting their hands on the sides of their head like they were sleeping and all sorts of things. And like they were grabbing bars and shaking them, but we just couldn't get it through our heads what they were trying to tell us and so Charlie went to the hoosegow again.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you know what it was for that time?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I don't have any idea.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: He kind of made it a regular habit though.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh yeah. We talked about the Chaffin place. Charlie hid out in the Chaffin place from the police. He had several little places that he hid out here and there and that was the way he knew this trail, this back trail through from Sulphur Springs, was trying to get away from police.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did he ever do any bootlegging or anything like that?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: He would have if he could have! I don't know that he did.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How would he stay alive. By poaching, or old orchards, or. .
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, I told you. . . there's another story I told you about that I don't think we got on tape was he worked for the Coote's mill, and Bill Coote owned it. And one day the sawyer was sick, and Charlie was setting ratchets, which was setting the carriage for the thickness of the lumber. And Bill Coote had had his forefinger cut off, so he'd hold up two fingers and Charlie set the ratchets for an inch and a half until noon
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Cause he was holding up one and a half fingers?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, he was holding one and a half fingers up, because he had that cut off finger! So Charlie he was cutting one and a half inch boards all morning until somebody caught on to what was going on. Charlie went down the road talking to himself! He got quite a few jobs.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Was he doing that just to be funny?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Just to be funny, yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Wasn't dense or anything.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, no, it just tickled him that Bill Coote was just holding up a finger and a half, so he sawed it a finger and a half. That was Charlie, he did love a joke. And he was a nice guy to be around, but like I say, I could have got into trouble chumming around with him because he was in trouble all the time.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now you told a story where he came up to that one place where he had stolen some beer bottles or something?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, that was the Parker's house. He came over and got me and says, "I want you to
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: go for a ride with me today. I'm going to go up in the hills." So, okay, I climbed in with him and we went up to Parker's place, and I was just sitting in the car. He got out and he had a whole bunch of beer bottles stashed away. We were only probably 75 feet from Parker's house. And Charlie started throwing them into the back of the car, and Mr. Parker came Out, and he was a good sized wood cutter, and he came out and he laid a log across the road and stood on top of the log with his arms folded, and he says, "Now unload all those." So Charlie unloaded them, but he broke a few of them. And when Charlie got them all unloaded, well, Mr. Parker got off the log and moved it out of the road, and he says, "Don't ever come back." I don't think Charlie ever did. Because he figured I was kind of a big kid, and I think he probably figured I'd be helpful to him. But I was a little bit nervous about that deal, I didn't like that at all.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How did he die?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, yeah, during World War II after he came back from the service, they moved over to . .. he had a sister who married a guy by the name of Pyburn over on Highway 20. And they built a house for Charlie's mother and father and him to live in. Which is about three or four miles this side of Albany. And Charlie got the measles and he thought it was funny, and he wouldn't go to bed or anything, and so finally he got real sick and got in bad shape with them, and he still thought it was kind of funny. And then his folks tried to get the doctor to come see him when he lost consciousness. And in those times nobody was going to waste their ration of gas to come out and see about a guy that was unconscious, and so he ultimately died right on their front porch. And the undertaker came out and got him. I think he was about 2 when he died.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Just a young man.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did he ever get married or have a girlfriend or anything?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, as far as I know, he never had any inclinations toward a girlfriend. I think he was too lazy, he didn't want to support one. But I will say this for Charlie, when Charlie came back after he got out of the penitentiary, he came up to my dad, and my dad was quite nervous when he saw him walking up. Charlie came up and he says, "I want to tell you that I'm sorry for what I did and I'd like to work for you to pay for the gas I stole." So he had some good parts to him and so forth.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I'm wondering, I see tractor tracks here, I'm wondering if Jeff's [Garver] been in here doing some work up and around the spring itself here. I also see two or three cars up there.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: We're just coming back from Sulphur Springs there, and you were telling me about these rocks here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, 1 was told that at one time the Sheriff of Benton County lived on past Sulphur Springs, and there was two things he didn't like about this set up. And one of them was cars driving all over it, and the other thing was vandalism and so forth. So apparently, he got some county dump trucks to pick up this rock, it looks like probably from the rock quarry over there by Wren, and dump some big rocks in here so that you couldn't get in with a car, to try to protect what was left of it. There has been a lot of motorcycle damage and since they built that new bridge on down the creek here a ways, well, they're asking everybody on horseback and motorcycle to go
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: around the beaver dam and come out on the road over that bridge, and stay out of this area and it sure looks like an improvement just from what I can see here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: You mean, in the last two years?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, the last two years. I think it was two years ago that I finally found that Jeff Garver had something to do with this, and in that two-year period I've seen he's done some cleaning up around Sulphur Springs itself, and put up signs and stuff. I'm feeling real good about it, I wish I could have followed this through to completion, but it looks like somebody's picked up the ball for me!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah, it's looking a lot nicer in the two years I've been coming here. Vandalism and horses.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, well, the horses and motorcycles and the bicycles were all coming through here. Apparently they got that stopped. And I have not seen any vandalism. When I came here a couple of years ago somebody had been living over there on the other side of the creek here, Soap Creek, and had some plastic tarps laying down there and one thing and another, and they just walked off and left. It was just looking awful trashy, and somebody's picked things up around here and so forth. So I'm real happy about it.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now we talked a little bit about some of the recommendations that they plant exotic grasses in here. Do you think that that's
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I wasn't in on the exotic grasses. Actually, I was too. Our office of the Soil and Water Conservation has been in with OSU on developing some grasses to use in the forests to help stop erosion, and we were talking about, I can't remember the name of that grass right now
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Brachopodium?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, that wasn't one of them.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's the one that they've got growing all through the forest now on the other side.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well this is newer grass. And it's not supposed to grow very high, to help the possibility of fire danger. This is a low, slow growing grass that just kind of grows along the ground, and . . . boy I can't think of the name of it. We planted some of it between 3rd and 4th Street there, where they come together on the north end of town as an experiment to see how it would work in this kind of a situation. And we just had it coming up well when I moved out of town, so I don't know how it worked.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's kind of a marsh area there, between 3rd and 4th. That was built up, so that would be a similar environment to here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Very similar, yeah. And that was the grass that I had suggested we plant here.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: What do you think f this had been used, maybe if they did start burning it and bring back wild strawberries and stuff, do you think that would be a good thing?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It might be a good thing, but I was thinking in terms of.. . nobody wants to mow it, that's why I was thinking of the short grass.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How about if they just came in like the Indians did and burned it every so often?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: You'd have weeping and wailing and gnashing of teeth with the environmentalists!
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: You think it would be a political issue.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, I think you'd run into, "Oh, we're blowing smoke in the air, and it's causing the greenhouse effect."
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: But what if it's bringing back the native wildflowers?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, well, they're not interested in that. Everybody has got their own hobby horse, you know.
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, so you think the smoke people and the wildflower people are two different camps?
entries.chapter_ref: V. Sulphur Springs and Charlie White

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, I think so!
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: We just got up to the top of the peak there, and I just took those panoramas, so we're coming downhill on the 700 road on the Oak Creek side; just left the Soap Creek side. And so when you and Charlie came through, you left at Sulphur Springs and crossed at Sulphur Springs and then you started up a ridgeline?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Urn hmm.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And how far did you go before you ran into the CCC boys? Oh, one question, did you ever call them the "3-C boys"?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, yeah, that's all they were ever called.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: "Three-C Boys".
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And not "CCC".
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh, sometimes, but I think more usually "3-C's". We're going to go left, huh?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah, I think so. 740 goes to the right. We'll try to the left. How many cows did you take over?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Those were all your father' s herd?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. And two horses and no saddles.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you and Charlie ride the horses?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We rode the horses bareback across.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So you left Berry Creek in the morning? Then how did you get from Berry Creek to Sulphur Springs?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Right down the gravel road. We left just at daybreak. Of course it was I think in probably January, and we got over to Oak Creek after dark with the cows. And we were pretty fortunate they moved right along, and we kept moving and I've often wondered how far it was across, between Sulphur Springs and Oak Creek. I think the road goes quite a bit further up Oak Creek than it did when we came across and Charlie thought we might run into a locked gate on the Oak Creek side, but we didn't. We were kind of afraid we might have to break the gate down because we sure weren't going to go back that night! And Charlie knew how to break gates down.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you know who owned the gate?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I have no idea.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you see anybody on your trip over?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, nothing but the CCC boys.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: When you saw them, how far from Sulphur Springs were they?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Probably a third of the way across.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: A third of the way towards Oak Creek?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Up on the ridge?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. But they were on the . . . actually not on the ridge, they were on the east side of the ridge, where they were working.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did you have any other contact with the 3-C's?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: My dad worked for them for a short while. There was.. . when they signed up I
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: think they signed up for a couple years. And my dad worked for the CCC's down in California some place and actually he was a boss. He kind of got to missing my mother after a couple weeks, and managed to get out. I never did know how he did that.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: He'd actually signed up as a 3-C member then?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And that's when you lived on Berry Creek?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, that was when we lived in California. Where he was in the CCC's was I think up around the Los Angeles County park, up at San Bernardino. So I knew about them before we ever moved up here. And this camp was fairly new when we moved up here. I don't know when they started them, but of course Roosevelt started them and he went in in 1932, then I imagine it took him a couple years to get some of these programs going. Social Security went into effect in 1936. That's where things were coming from. What are we looking at over there?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: If I'm not too lost, we should be looking across Alder Creek towards Philomath. If I'm too lost we're looking at Kings Valley or Albany.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Or Portland!
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So you drove 27 head of cows and. . . do you call them cows or cattle?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Cattle.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How many of them were milk cows?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: All of them were either milk cows or heifers. We didn't take any bulls across.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Then you moved them to where your family was moving in 1939?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I believe it was '40.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Just the year before Adair, then.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Can you recall any incidents along the trail, other than seeing the 3-C's?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, we just followed the cows and the cows followed the trail and we just kept pushing them about as fast as we could keep them walking. When we got there and got the cows in the barn and went in the house to eat supper, my mother had supper ready and my dad was still over at the other farm, and we were sitting there eating and all at once the dining room window started going up. And it went clear up to the top and everybody was holding their breath, but it stopped there and there was nobody around. It just happened that in those days they had sash weights to open the window and the weights were heavier than the window was, so with us vibrating the house well it just started going up! Scared the daylights out of us!
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Oh, so that's when you and Charlie had first gotten into the house there?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, we'd just got in the house and my mother was there. And she'd cooked supper and we all sat down at the dining room table and just as we started to serve that window goes up very slowly. Now we're looking at some country we ought to know!
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah, let's see, we're on the Patterson Road, on the 600 Road, and we've moved west from Lewisburg Saddle, and we're overlooking Corvallis through this clearcut here.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't know what those big houses are down there. I saw them from up on top of that high peak.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's gotta be Oregon State, doesn't it? Or is it?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't think so. That's north of Oregon State quite a ways.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Could that be the hospital?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, might be the horse barns or something like that.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: You were talking about knowing Bill Wheeler.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Okay. I met Bill Wheeler at Northwest Hills Church where Jeff also goes, and Bill Wheeler's a real likeable guy. And we just hit it off real good together. He's not quite as big as I am, but he's pretty chunky and always got a smile and a laugh and so forth, and he was of course a professor up there in the Forestry Department. Apparently my son took a class under him. But he came out from Minnesota on a kind of a sabbatical for a year or two, and he decided he didn't want to go back to Minnesota. So he got a permanent teaching job here. And I've got a boat and he's got a boat just exactly like mine, and we've gone out fishing a few times together. Unfortunately he's had boat motor problems and he was quite amazed at how fast I could fix his boat for him. And anyway, we went up to his house one time for a visit and coffee, his wife makes real good apple pie, and he invited us up for apple pie and coffee, and a visit. And so when he told me where he lived, well I told him you've got to live awfully close to where I used to live on Oak Creek. So when we got there, I looked out his front window, and I says, "See that barn right down there straight below us?" He says, "Yeah." I says, "That used to be our barn!" So if we get over on Oak Creek early enough, before it gets pretty dark, I'll show you where we lived and where Tortora's live and where old Bill Wheeler lives.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Does Bill Wheeler still live there?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yes. Now where do we go?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Says 600 road to the right there. Did Bill Wheeler ever talk about his work with the College of Forestry?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: A little bit. Really he's not a bragger or anything, and every once in a while we'll run into people that we know, mutual friends and stuff, he'll say, "Oh, yeah, I had him in my class" or something like that. But really he didn't. . . I think mainly he was just a teacher not a guy that was out looking around and writing books. However, from his house he walks clear up here past the Oak Creek gate every day. He and his wife walk about four miles a day and they walk up here. And try to keep healthy and so forth. But he's been retired now for seven or eight years.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: When you say you 'ye got the same kind of boats, would you go fishing?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Yeah, we've got Bayliners with 50 horse Evinrudes on them. His is a Johnson and mine's an Evinrude, but they're identical.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Where do you go fishing at?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We used to go fishing up on Foster. I fished Foster quite a few years and I fished there long enough my dad and I developed a . . . changed a lure that you can buy in the store and I can normally go up there and take two guys with me and limit out in two hours or less. And anyway, so, we went up there several times and we'd get up there about 8:00 or so, he and another guy and I. I was always the pilot because the guy that brought the boat and the motor, the other two guys were supposed to buy him dinner in that restaurant there. If we didn't limit out by noon. So when I started to see we were getting to close to limit, well I'd try to knock them off those guys so we wouldn't get limited out until afternoon so I'd get my free dinner! Because if we
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: limited out at 9:30 or so, we just loaded up the boat and went home. But anyway, that was . . . I fish with a triple teaser and I found that I could bend them to make them dart instead of just spin. And they're really effective. It was kind of interesting one time I was up there fishing, and came in at 10:00 and there was a guy camped next to us so I asked him how he was doing, he had three boys there, and he says, "Oh, just like everybody else, not catching a thing. I don't even fish, just the boys fish." So I says, well, let me give you a lure for the boys to fish. So I gave him one that I'd fixed up you know, and towards noon I came in and he was there, he was waiting for me and he says, "I can't figure it out. We no more than dropped that hook in the water, and we had a fish on. We were just catching one after another."
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: This the road you were coming in on?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, this is right about where we were coming through. Right in here.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah, this should have been it. You should have been coming down the ridge and then they'd be tapering down right about through here.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: So anyway, he says, "Man, we just caught fish to beat the band on that setup of yours! I went back to Sweet Home and went into the tackle shop and said 'I want four riggings, just like this.' And they made up four riggings identical to this, but we can't catch anything except on yours!" He says, "We can't see what's different." I says, "Well, you just watch and I'll show you." So I bent those four of his and took mine back. When I came in that evening . . . now mind you, they only have three boys, but he was standing there on the dock bragging about how all four of them limited out. And he told me he wasn't fishing. All at once he got into it.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So Bill Wheeler, was he like a fishing buddy of yours pretty much?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Yeah, I've got a picture of Bill Wheeler and Dean Webb was a dentist, and I with a limit of fish. Dean Webb took the picture, he just got a new camera that he could set and get the picture of himself too. I was up to Bill Wheeler's house about a month ago. By the time we got this far with that herd of cows, we still had three or four miles to go and we were getting pretty antsy to get home. Cause it was probably about this dark when we were here, and we still had a ways to go.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Did your folks drive around the other side to meet you?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Oh yeah. My mother did. My mother drove around to meet us and she also . . . see this is where the horses are really tearing things up.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: See the beaver ponds through here? This is all pretty new. That grass growing up through those trees there, that's that Brachopodiun. I don't know what the deal is there, i've never seen grass grow so much underneath fir trees before. Here 's the road we're going to come into right here, one goes up toward the old homestead and one. . . that would have been the 680 coming down to the 600 here.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Getting roads all over here, huh.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yeah. There used to be a mill down through this area. In fact the school owned it.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: 'What's all this?
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I'm not sure. It's some kind of testing on grass or something. They've got sediment tests through here, and they've got quite a bit of research through this area here.
entries.chapter_ref: W. The Oak Creek—Sulphur Springs Trail

chapters.title: Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School
chapters.label: Y.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't think we have to worry about seeing Bill Wheeler walking on this road, because they do their walking about 8:30 in the morning.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Seen plenty of other people, though. Seen four or five hikers and ten or twelve bikers.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Looks to me like somebody's walking their dogs, too.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: X. The Oak Creek Gate
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Quite a few people out here for having locked gates.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: That's what Garver was telling me, that he just can't believe the people that come up in here.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: There's an old orchard right through here and the beaver have been knocking the trees down left and right.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The beaver, you say?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Yep. You can see it down through there, you can see some of the trees we've flagged there. But some of the others down there . . . you can see the pond right there.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Of course there wasn't any beavers when I came here.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: This is probably the gate right here.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: A metal gate? And you think that was there?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I think that was probably the gate we were worried about but it was open.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Right at the end of the.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I think that was a private gate, I don't know for sure.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: You don't recall any houses or anything?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: There was no houses up here. We drove the cattle down this way for quite a ways before we got into any sign of any habitation at all.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do you recognize anything through here at all?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, we didn't see any sign of habitation for. . . I can't figure those buildings being CCC buildings.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And not having been here when you came through?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's something I'm kind of curious about too. That's why I was asking.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: We didn't see any habitation until we got down here into the farming area.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Well, Royal Jackson asked Edward Sekermestrovich about that vely thing, and he said that he couldn't remember them building any buildings, and he was in the CCC's until the '40s.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, now, maybe I was a little bit turned around here. Is this the road here that goes on up to the old post road?
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: No. This one might be a development. That one I think is a little further down here.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, that's right.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: We were just at Tanager, and I think it's called Skunk Creek Road.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: But it was down in about here before we saw any signs of habitation. Where it started to widen out here.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: There's Skillings Road, I think that's a fairly old road.
entries.chapter_ref: Y. Skunk Creek Road and Oak Creek School

chapters.title: The Tortora House and Raising Kids
chapters.label: Z.

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, Skillings used to keep you from going up into the forest there with his rifle. I met him one time with a rifle.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: There's an old orchard here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Yeah, Skillings was a little bit on the mean side. I came out from up there on Oak Creek, I went in this way and I burned out a coil, so I walked out Skillings Road. Now the old [Oak Creek] school house set right in there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, now we're right on the corner of Cardwell Hill Road. And the school house set on this corner right here?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, right here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, about where the old cyclone fence is?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Where all these old trees are and stuff.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Where that holly is there. Is that associated with the school somehow?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't know.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So the school was right in there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Right in there, yeah. Just real close to the creek there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And you called that Oak Creek school?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. Of course, this was all gravel road then.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And from the school up that way, only Skillings lived up that way?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, there were several. I'm talking about 15 years ago, I'm not talking about when I lived here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Oh, I see, so Skillings was there only 15 years ago.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, that's the first I ever heard of him.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, so when you lived here, did anybody live up that way at all?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: I don't really know. I didn't come up this way very much. I herded cows down and I went to Corvallis. So I couldn't tell you.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So when Skillings accosted you, you were an adult. You weren't a kid then anymore.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No. Now Tortoras lived in that house right there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, that's the white house here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: heading
entries.text: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, we're right next to an electrical substation.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, that wasn't there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And it's got red trim on it. How about that big old red barn up on the hill there?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: That's our barn.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Oh, I've been wanting to know the story on this for some time.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, that's all I know about it. It's a three-story barn. And we only lived there for six or eight months. But that was our barn. And Bill Wheeler lives in the next house that sits up on the bank like that one.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I stopped and talked to the people here that have this barn one day. I was tracing the Applegate Trail right through this area.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah. When we lived here, there was no electricity here. This is where you turn to go up to Bill Wheeler's.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: His is the brown house there?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Yeah, this is his house right here. Now this was all our pasture.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Up on the hill there.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: This whole hill. Clear down to the valley. But I chased those cotton-pickin' cows all over this hillside. But our pasture went . . . see that was our fields down there. And our pasture went over two rises and valleys and you can imagine climbing these cotton-pickin' hills. See there's one of the low spots, then this is the next ridge here. But you see how steep that is?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Were any. . . we're on Ridgewood Drive here. Was there a road through here?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, this was just slrictly our pasture. We had a fence around it and that was it. Our place and Tortora's place had adjoining fences, but there was absolutely no . . . I mean this was just pasture.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Who did you get your house from?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Guy by the name of Crane. We rented it from him and . . . see our pasture went clear down into the bottom of this canyon here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So the reason you didn't know any of the neighbors around here is there wasn't any.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: There wasn't any! This was all native grass and rose bushes.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Do they call it sweet briar? Or just call it rose bushes?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: It was always wild roses.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Then on the blackberries, I'm kind of curious, you call them wild mountain blackberries, for those trailing blackberries, the natives. And then the himalayas, were those considered natives, or
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No way. They were brought in by the settlers. And actually when I moved to Oregon they were still in rows. You didn't see them just growing all over like now.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: How about the evergreen blackberries?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Well, I'm pretty sure they were brought in too. Because they were pretty much under a cultivated status.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Now we're looking at Bald Hill right there, right?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Bald Hill, right.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: That's interesting. Right where your old place was and that barn was one trail that the Applegate Trail I was tracking out. I was real curious who owned that barn, I went and talked to the people there but they didn't know much about it.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Were they renters?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: I think so.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: Okay, I talked to the renters that were in that house a couple of years ago, and they told me that the owners were going to move in that fall.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay, it was a couple years ago when I was doing it.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: And they were telling me that they were sure that the owner would just be tickled to death to talk to me and hear some history on the old place.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: This is where the Applegate Trail went to the north side of Bald Hill here.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: See how Wheeler's looking right down on our barn?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: And you lived in the old. . . was that house yellow at that time?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: No, I think it was white.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: Okay. And then that little house wasn't even in there, right?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: The little house wasn't in there, but there was a lot of buildings in there. There was a row of three big chicken houses in here, and I raised chickens. And this little building that sticks out behind the house there, we had a koller light plant in there, and we couldn't afford batteries for it, so we never ran it. We used our kerosine lamps and stuff. But on Thanksgiving and Christmas when all my brothers and sisters and
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
entries.text: brother-in-laws would come -- it took 32 volts to start it, 36 volts I guess -- and we all had six volt batteries in our cars, so we had to get six batteries together to get enough to start it. And when we'd hook up all the batteries to it, all we had to do was turn on a light switch any place in the house and that power plant would start up. The way it was set up the batteries completed the circuit through the light and made the power plant start up.
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: Q
entries.text: So you'd just start the power plant for special occasions then?
entries.chapter_ref: Z. The Tortora House and Raising Kids

entries.speaker: A
